civil-service-commission.note: Civil Service Act 1917 made the commission report to the Provincial Secretary; the Provincial Secretary still administered it in 1947. Not confirmed after 1947.

public-library-commission.note: The commission was renamed the Library Development Commission in April 1968.

labour-relations-board-1947.note: Funded through the Department of Labour's vote from 1947 and under its Labour Relations Branch from 1954. The Labour Code of 1973 made it independent, but it still reported directly to the Minister of Labour. The department was renamed the Ministry of Labour in 1976 (OIC 3199/76).

bc-toll-highways-and-bridges-authority.note: Under the Toll Highways and Bridges Authority Act (SBC 1953 2nd Sess. c. 37; RSBC 1960 c. 380, s. 13), the authority gave its annual report to the Minister of Finance, who laid it before the Legislature.

bc-railway-company.note: BC Rail is listed under the Ministry of Transportation in the January 2004 and June 2005 cabinet-responsibility lists. The 2005/06–2008/09 service plans are addressed to the Minister of Transportation, who was also Minister Responsible for the British Columbia Railway Company.

The 2009 service plan is addressed to the Minister of Transportation and Infrastructure. BC Rail is listed under this ministry in 2009 and 2010. The company's own site still calls it a subsidiary of BCTFA under this ministry. The end date is when the ministry was renamed.

human-rights-commission-1973.note: Under the Human Rights Code (SBC 1973 c. 119), the Minister of Labour appointed the director, received the annual report and acted as the commission's fiscal agent. BC Archives lists the commission among the bodies reporting directly to the Minister of Labour.
The department was renamed the Ministry of Labour in 1976 (OIC 3199/76). In 1984, Minister of Labour Robert McClelland described himself as 'the minister responsible for the Human Rights Commission'.

bc-heritage-trust.note: The Trust was constituted under Part IV of the Heritage Conservation Act. For every period of this body, the ministry recorded is the one that administered that Act and the Heritage Conservation Branch the Trust worked with.

bc-heritage-trust.ministry: Ministry of Provincial Secretary and Government Services
bc-heritage-trust.note: This ministry acquired the Heritage Conservation Act in 1978.

bc-heritage-trust.ministry: Ministry of Tourism, Recreation and Culture
bc-heritage-trust.note: Historic-resource functions were moved here in 1986 (OIC 1908/86).

bc-heritage-trust.ministry: Ministry of Municipal Affairs, Recreation and Culture
Ministry of Small Business, Tourism and Culture
Ministry of Community, Aboriginal and Women's Services

science-council-of-bc.ministry: Ministry of Advanced Education, Training and Technology
science-council-of-bc.note: The auditors' report on the 1997/98 financial statements is addressed to the Minister of Advanced Education, Training and Technology.

science-council-of-bc.ministry: Ministry of Competition, Science and Enterprise
science-council-of-bc.note: The 2003 service plan says the council is funded through this ministry, which lasted from 2001 to 2004.

science-council-of-bc.ministry: Ministry of Small Business and Economic Development
science-council-of-bc.note: Listed as the 'Innovation and Science Council of BC'.

bc-utilities-commission.ministry: Ministry of Energy, Mines and Petroleum Resources
bc-utilities-commission.note: When this ministry was disestablished in 1996 (OIC 197/96), its Utilities Commission functions were kept out of the transfer to the Ministry of Employment and Investment.
Listed under the Attorney General in 2004, 2005, 2009 and 2010.

BCUC appointments were recommended by the 'Attorney General and Minister of Justice' (OIC 641/2013, 646/2014, 733/2015). BC Archives says the ministry was called the Ministry of Justice from 2012 to 2017.
The Attorney General recommended the chair appointments in OIC 295/2018, 490/2019, 525/2023 and 114/2025. Policy directions under s. 3 come from the energy minister (for example OIC 131/2025).

council-of-human-rights.note: The 1984 Human Rights Act, which created the Council, was brought in and promoted by Minister of Labour Robert McClelland. Responsibility from 1985 to 1991 is not confirmed.
Anita Hagen held this through the portfolio of Minister Responsible for Multiculturalism and Human Rights.

council-of-human-rights.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks
council-of-human-rights.note: Moe Sihota held this through the portfolio of Minister Responsible for Multiculturalism and Human Rights.
Ujjal Dosanjh held this through the portfolio of Minister Responsible for Multiculturalism and Human Rights.
Ujjal Dosanjh, as Attorney General, was Minister Responsible for Multiculturalism, Human Rights and Immigration.

first-peoples-cultural-council.ministry: Ministry of Community, Aboriginal and Women's Services
first-peoples-cultural-council.note: The 2004/05 service plan letter is addressed to Murray Coell, Minister of Community, Aboriginal and Women's Services, and the council is listed under that ministry in January 2004.

first-peoples-cultural-council.ministry: Ministry of Aboriginal Relations and Reconciliation
first-peoples-cultural-council.note: Service-plan letters are addressed to this minister in 2006 and in every year from 2009 to 2014.

first-peoples-cultural-council.ministry: Ministry of Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation
first-peoples-cultural-council.note: Mandate letters in the 2022–2026 service plans come from the Minister of Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation.

forest-renewal-bc.note: Under the Forest Renewal Act, the Minister of Forests approved committee appointments, could require accounts and laid the reports before the Legislature. The Minister of Finance and Corporate Relations was fiscal agent only.

bc-arts-council.ministry: Ministry of Community, Aboriginal and Women's Services
Ministry of Small Business and Economic Development
Ministry of Tourism, Sport and the Arts
Ministry of Tourism, Culture and the Arts
Ministry of Community, Sport and Cultural Development
bc-arts-council.note: BC Archives places the council in this ministry as of 2016.

bc-arts-council.ministry: Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture
bc-arts-council.note: The minister made council appointments in January 2018 and tabled the 2018/19 annual report in October 2019.

bc-arts-council.ministry: Ministry of Tourism, Arts, Culture and Sport
bc-arts-council.note: The council's publications page links this ministry's 2022/23–2026/27 service plans.

regional-health-boards-1997.ministry: Ministry of Health and Ministry Responsible for Seniors
regional-health-boards-1997.note: The ministry had this name from 1996 (OIC 203/96) until it was split in 2001. The attribution is inferred: the boards were created under the Health Authorities Act, which this ministry administered. No source names the boards' minister directly.
After the 2001 split, this ministry was responsible for standards and direction for health authorities.

bc-investment-management-corporation.ministry: Ministry of Finance and Corporate Relations
bc-investment-management-corporation.note: Under the Public Sector Pension Plans Act (SBC 1999 c. 44), BCI's single share is held by the Minister of Finance. In 1999 that portfolio was titled Minister of Finance and Corporate Relations.
Listed as 'BC Investment Management Corporation' under Finance in January 2004. The share is still held by the Minister of Finance under the Act.

northern-health.note: 'Regional Health Authorities' are listed under Health Services in January 2004.
The 2020/21 financial statements say the board is appointed by the Ministry of Health.

partnerships-bc.note: Every service plan from 2003 to 2020 names the Minister of Finance as sole shareholder. The body is listed under Finance in 2004, 2005, 2009 and 2010.

industry-training-authority.note: The 2005/06 service plan is addressed to Ida Chong, Minister of Advanced Education.

industry-training-authority.ministry: Ministry of Advanced Education and Labour Market Development
Ministry of Regional Economic and Skills Development
Ministry of Jobs, Tourism and Innovation
Ministry of Jobs, Tourism and Skills Training
industry-training-authority.note: The 2013 and 2014 plans are addressed to this minister. The 2015–2017 plans name no minister.

industry-training-authority.ministry: Ministry of Advanced Education, Skills and Training
Ministry of Advanced Education and Skills Training
industry-training-authority.note: The July 2021 mandate letter came from the minister responsible for ITA. The body was renamed SkilledTradesBC in December 2022.

community-living-bc.ministry: Ministry of Children and Family Development
community-living-bc.note: The interim CLBC board was already under this ministry in January 2004. The 2006–2008 service plans are addressed to the Minister of Children and Family Development.

community-living-bc.ministry: Ministry of Housing and Social Development
Ministry of Social Development and Social Innovation
Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction

transportation-investment-corporation.note: The 2010/11 plan says the board reports to the Minister of Transportation and Infrastructure, who is designated Minister Responsible for TI Corp. Plans from 2011 to 2023 say the same.

technical-safety-bc.ministry: Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing
technical-safety-bc.note: The Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing appointed a board member in December 2017. In 2019 TSBC filed regulatory amendment requests with this ministry.
A 2021–22 performance audit was done for the 'Ministry of Attorney General and Ministry responsible for Housing', and the Attorney General held the Minister Responsible for Housing portfolio.

inbc.ministry: Ministry of Jobs, Economic Recovery and Innovation
inbc.note: The InBC Investment Corp. Act requires annual reports to the Minister of Jobs, Economic Recovery and Innovation.

inbc.ministry: Ministry of Jobs, Economic Development and Innovation
Ministry of Jobs and Economic Growth

bc-family-maintenance-agency.note: The 2022/23 and 2023/24 mandate letters came from the Attorney General, who was also Minister Responsible for Housing. The gov.bc.ca page (2025) names the Ministry of Attorney General.

gaps: civil-service-commission: 1947–1973 not confirmed. It was presumably still under the Provincial Secretary, but no source says so.
labour-relations-board-1947: 1976–1987 (Ministry of Labour, then Ministry of Labour and Consumer Services) not confirmed by a source naming the Board.
bc-electric-company-crown (1961-08-01 to 1962-03-31): no source found naming the minister or ministry. The Power Development Act 1961 text was not retrieved.

bc-railway-company: 1972–2003 not found. No source was retrieved for the Barrett, Bennett, Vander Zalm, Harcourt or Clark eras. The 2003 service plan names no minister. The 2024-11-18 rename to Transportation and Transit is not confirmed for BCRC.

provincial-land-commission (1973–1978): the Land Commission Act gave it to 'the member of the Executive Council charged by Order in Council', and that OIC was not found. The Minister of Agriculture, Stupich, is associated with the Act, but no source designates him.
human-rights-commission-1973: covered for 1973–1984. The 1976–1982 part rests on the Code naming the Minister of Labour.

bc-steamship-company (1975–1992): not found. Lands Minister Robert Williams announced its creation in 1975. BC Archives links it hierarchically, without dates, to the Ministry of Small Business, Tourism and Culture (1993–2001), which is after the company dissolved.
bc-heritage-trust: every period is attributed through the ministry administering the Heritage Conservation Act and Heritage Conservation Branch. No source names the Trust's minister directly.

science-council-of-bc: 1978–1997 and 1998–2001 not found. The council was probably under Education, Science and Technology (1978–79) and then Universities, Science and Communications (1979–86), but no source names it.

metro-transit-operating-company (1979–1983): no source found. Vander Zalm, as Minister of Municipal Affairs, is reported as responsible for the Urban Transit Authority in 1978, but his ministry gave up transportation during 1978–82, and MTOC itself is not tied to any minister.
bc-utilities-commission: 1996–2003 not found. OIC 197/96 kept UC functions out of the transfer to Employment and Investment, but the receiving ministry is not stated.

council-of-human-rights: 1985–1991 (Labour, then Labour and Consumer Services) not confirmed. 1991–1997 rests on the 'Minister Responsible for Multiculturalism and Human Rights' portfolio, not a portfolio named for the Council.
first-peoples-cultural-council: 1990–2003 not found. The Minister of Native Affairs in 1990 was Jack Weisgerber, but no source ties the council to that ministry.
bc-arts-council: 1995–2003 not found. The Cultural Services Branch, secretariat to the predecessor Arts Board, was in the Ministry of Small Business, Tourism and Culture from 1996.
transportation-investment-corporation: 2008–2009 not directly sourced. The earliest source is the 2010 service plan.
technical-safety-bc: from 2022-12-07 not found (presumably Ministry of Housing, then Ministry of Housing and Municipal Affairs).
industry-training-authority: 2022-12-07 to its end in December 2022 (Ministry of Post-Secondary Education and Future Skills) is not separately sourced.

first-nations-health-authority: no provincial answering ministry. FNHA is a First Nations-governed body under the 2011 BC Tripartite Framework Agreement, and the Ministry of Health is only a tripartite partner. Recorded no period.
regional-health-boards-1997: the ministry is inferred from the ministry that administered the Health Authorities Act. No source names the boards' minister directly.
